title: Eval system: deterministic PII signal matching
description:
Add deterministic evaluation of PII signal rules after the shared evaluator lands.

Blocked only on DATAP-c7dd46 shared evaluator contract. Once c7dd46 lands, proceeds in PARALLEL with DATAP-d61496. Real benchmark cases from DATAP-b17f92 supplement committed smoke fixtures and the versioned third-party benchmark when available (optional enrichment, not a start blocker).

First extract existing lexical rule matching into a pure reusable deterministic function with explicit hit identity, category, matched evidence, file path, and line range. The evaluation may call that matcher directly with AI disabled.

Do not automatically place PII hits into default scan output. Exposing a new output collection or running the pass by default changes product behavior, schema, runtime, and false-positive surface; track that as a separate product decision.

Evaluate recall, conditional label accuracy, correct-label recall, true precision within exhaustively annotated scopes, negative-case pass rate, and per-file unread counts. Use both committed smoke fixtures and the versioned third-party benchmark.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Eval system: PII signal matching (Layer 3)

Follow-up PR. This one requires a minimal scanner change.

### What it evaluates

The scanner has PII signal rules (patterns/pii-signals.rules.yaml) — lexical regex for sensitive data like SSN, email, card numbers. On main, these rules are used ONLY inside buildThirdPartyDataFlowSummary() to enrich data flows with privacy categories, gated behind enableAiInference: true + aiThirdPartyDataFlowEnabled: true (both off by default).

This layer evaluates whether the PII regex rules correctly identify sensitive data in source files — as standalone findings, not just as data-flow enrichment.

### Minimal scanner change required

Extract the PII regex matching from the AI-gated path into a standalone deterministic pass:

- The regex rules themselves are deterministic (no LLM)
- Currently they only run when AI is enabled and third-party data flow is enabled
- The change: apply the regex rules in a deterministic scan stage that runs regardless of AI flags
- This makes PII signal detection evaluable without LLM

This is a small but real scanner change — pulling existing logic out from behind a feature flag into the default path. It does not add new detection logic; it un-gates existing logic.

### Adapter

Maps PII regex hits → ReportedFinding[]:

```typescript
const findings: ReportedFinding[] = piiHits.map(hit => ({
  name: hit.matchedText,
  labels: [hit.category],
  evidence: [{ filePath: hit.filePath, startLine: hit.line, endLine: hit.line }],
}));
```

### Cases

- Recall: "expect ssn regex hit at user.py line 5 labelled user_identity_direct"
- Precision: "expect NO PII hit at config.py line 10" (non-sensitive field with a similar name)
- Label accuracy: "expect the hit to be labelled as the correct PII category"

### Scope

- Minimal scanner change: un-gate PII regex matching from AI path
- New adapter + cases under tests/eval/layers/pii-signals/
- No LLM (the regex rules are deterministic)
- Follow-up to the Layer 1 PR (depends on the shared scoring engine landing first)

## Status vs PR #3 (2026-08-27)

Deterministic PII matcher extraction (`src/pii-signals/`) is on [#3](https://github.com/DataParade-io/dataparade-cli/pull/3). Keep **open until #3 merges**.

T0 provisional corpus run (2026-08-27, proposed states): 15 YAML rules, ~37% recall, **0% label accuracy** — taxonomy/identity mismatch, not a broken matcher. Label aliases + location-first identity are the T1 scoring-contract follow-up, not extra regex in this issue.
